main_text.l: ARTICULUS IX.
SAtis erat probasse eum radium esse corporeum,
& congruere rationi & experientiæ, si minutissi-
ma corpuscula ab aëre raro non moverentur. Ne-
que solùm experientiæ ipsi, argumentisque ab
ea ductis, satisfecimus, quod respondentis erat offici-
um. Sed ejusdem experientiæ manu, indissolubili-
bus rationum nodis Adversarios constrinximus,
nostramque, ac Veterum sententiam certissimam feci-
mus, radiorum motu in aqua manifestum reddente
eos esse corporeos. Cujus experimenti, rationisque
vim nulla protervia possit effugere. Cæterum
demonstrare quomodo fiat, ut his radiis intactis,
aër transeat humani ingenii vires transcendere videba-
tur. Conati tamen sumus hujus probabilem ali-
quam facere declarationem: Talem fecimus quæ
cuivis æquo judici sufficiat. Pendantur dicta &
sufficit.
INTENTIO V.
Quid sint illi radii visiles, & an
ignei sint.
ARTICULUS I.
NUnc videndum est, an quod diximus verum fit, id scilicet quod
ex oculis profilit esse igneum, ex cujus probatione, magis dictoru-
m veri-

page.notes: The first word of the lower paragraph is a drop cap: "NUnc" is transcribed as N and Vnc joined, with the v read as u. The head "ARTICVLVS" is read as ARTICULUS (vowel u). The printed "fcilicet" is read as scilicet (long s). The printed "profilit" is kept as printed. The page-number and running-head forms are from the top margin. The signature "Mm" and catchword "veri-" are at the foot. No doubtful readings.
